todo_line: - [ ] 001 Record the architecture decision before further implementation.
outcome: Revise ADR 0025 so provider acceptance survives replay, historic follow provenance is temporally proved, sibling reconciliation grants cannot suppress one another, and every revocation consequence has deterministic append order.
scope: Revise only `docs/adr/0025-use-first-class-group-memberships-and-member-owned-conversation-subscriptions.md`, preserving its accepted status and every settled first-class membership, member-owned subscription, root/reply ordering, delivery cutover, authorization, revocation-receipt, and reconciliation rule not implicated by the latest review.

Make provider acceptance durable and replayable for both legacy and provenance-aware private deliveries. Name the fact, ledger record, or equivalent rebuild-preservation mechanism; define its owner, required identity/correlation payload, append or persistence point relative to the external provider response, exact retry and restart behavior, and the recovery rule for the provider-accepted/crash-before-local-record window. A projection rebuild must not turn already-provider-accepted work back into pending or allow a second handoff.

Extend the private-delivery cutover protocol to classify already-provider-accepted legacy deliveries from durable replayable evidence, including the disposition of currently `sent` operational rows before the fence. Do not treat a mutable projection-only `sent` update as rebuild-safe evidence, and do not reclassify provider-accepted work as ineligible.

Require temporal proof for every historic custom-group follow candidate. The decisive effective legacy follow fact must be durably ordered inside the final uninterrupted legacy admission interval represented by the reconciled current membership: after the interval-opening `GroupMemberAdded`, with no later `GroupMemberRemoved` through the fence. State the comparable event-position evidence used across Membership and Messaging. If the source facts cannot prove that relationship, append the deterministic `unproved` result rather than binding the follow to whichever membership happens to be current at the fence.

Fix multi-provenance historic reconciliation so independently applicable sibling candidates for one person/conversation relation are evaluated without grants produced earlier in the same reconciliation batch suppressing later siblings. Define one atomic aggregate-local command/decision or an equally explicit pre-batch-state rule, deterministic candidate/grant/marker ordering, and event-free exact retry. Preserve the reviewed precedence for genuinely pre-existing canonical state, unfollow tombstones, and exact relevant revocations.

Complete the revocation append contract with total sort keys for prepared-intent cancellations and authorization-end facts. Keep the existing membership-wide tombstone first, per-grant provenance consequences, cancellations, grant ends, and completion receipt last; specify deterministic ordering within every zero-or-more consequence class so map/set iteration cannot change replayed event order.
scope_exclusions: Do not change application code, migrations, tests, feature files, acceptance tags, designs, ADR index entries, iteration files, todo lines, or runtime behavior in this packet.

Do not reopen the Club aggregate boundary, fresh group-membership identity, one-current-membership invariant, creator admission, club-departure end set, conditional root auto-follow, immutable subscription-grant model, server-resolved provenance, provider-handoff authority check, or receipt-based removal completion already settled in ADR 0025.

Do not restore projection-only provider acceptance, current-access fallback for legacy work, conversation cleanup fan-out, projection enumeration, reusable membership activation, or `MessageSent` as an independently replayed live follow fact.
Do not infer historic follow provenance from fence-time membership alone, timestamps without a durable total order, a later re-addition, or an ambiguous source interval.
Do not change the task identity, reset revision history, promote any candidate ADR revision to accepted task evidence, or implement tasks 002-025.

references.facts: Implementation Plan steps 1, 2, 4-6, and 8 require a binding replay-safe architecture, conservative reconciliation, immutable subscription authorization, durable revocation, exact provider-handoff eligibility, and restart/race coverage.

The current revise verdict identifies exactly four remaining gaps: projection-only provider acceptance, missing final-admission temporal proof, same-batch sibling reconciliation suppression, and unspecified ordering for revocation-time cancellation and grant-end facts.

The current accepted candidate already defines the delivery fence and legacy ineligibility fact, final-handoff authorization, immutable multi-grants, historic reconciliation table, and revocation append groups. Revise those sections narrowly to close the latest four gaps without discarding settled contracts.
The Message aggregate owns each delivery state machine and stream, which constrains where a replayable provider-acceptance fact or its explicitly justified equivalent belongs.
Provider acceptance, migration outcomes, and reconciliation decisions must remain reconstructible from immutable durable facts; projections and snapshots are not source-of-truth substitutes.

`mark_delivery_sent/2` currently records provider acceptance only with `Repo.update_all/2` on the email-delivery projection. A crash/rebuild can therefore lose the acceptance outcome even though the provider call already succeeded.
Replay of every historic `EmailDeliveryCreated` inserts a `pending` row and has no provider-acceptance event handler, demonstrating the rebuild hole named by review.
`EmailDeliveryCreated` contains message, delivery, and recipient fields but no provider-acceptance identity or outcome; creation is not durable proof that an external provider accepted the delivery.
Accepted tests verify provider success updates a row to `sent` and later access loss leaves that row untouched, but do not supply replayable acceptance evidence after projection rebuild.

The legacy start fact identifies club, group, reusable club membership, and person but has no first-class admission identity; its durable event position must delimit any provable final uninterrupted admission interval.

The legacy removal fact uses the same reusable relation identity, so remove/re-add histories require source ordering rather than fence-time current state to prove which admission contained a historic follow.

Historic `MessageSent` may establish an effective follow, including default-true legacy shapes, but carries no group-membership provenance; reconciliation must correlate its durable position conservatively with the final uninterrupted admission.
Historic explicit follow facts identify person, club, and conversation but no group-membership admission, so current-at-fence membership alone cannot prove temporal provenance.
Historic explicit unfollow contributes to the decisive effective legacy relation and must be included when selecting the exact follow fact whose admission interval is proved.

Membership and Messaging use their respective Commanded applications and configured EventStore adapters; the ADR must name the durable comparable event-position contract used for cross-context temporal proof rather than relying on wall-clock timestamps.

constraints: Keep ADR 0025 status `accepted`; the approved plan has no open business decision and executable work remains blocked on a complete architecture record.
Use concrete command, event, marker, or ledger names and define ownership, payload, cardinality, ordering, idempotency, and restart/rebuild behavior for every revised protocol.

Provider-accepted means the external handoff already succeeded and cannot be recalled. Its durable evidence must prevent both projection-rebuild regression to `pending` and duplicate provider handoff, including the crash boundary between provider response and local persistence.
The delivery cutover may preserve legacy accepted work, but it must not manufacture exact creation-time authorization for old pending work or use current access after remove/re-add as proof.

Historic custom-group authorization is provable only when the decisive effective follow fact is durably located within the final uninterrupted legacy admission interval. Missing, incomparable, or ambiguous order is `unproved`.

Sibling reconciliation candidates must retain independent provenance. Grants and markers emitted for one sibling in the current atomic batch are not pre-existing canonical state and cannot suppress another valid sibling.

Revocation event order must be a pure function of aggregate state and command data. Specify total keys for provenance-removal facts, prepared-intent cancellations, and grant-end facts, with the one completion receipt last.
Retain append-only compatibility and do not rewrite historic events, invent unproved membership periods, or treat read projections as aggregate/domain completion evidence.
This is documentation-only, so do not run `dev check`, `dev check --quick`, `dev ci`, or another full-suite command.
focused_validation: Review the final ADR against all four gaps in `.delivery/latest-review.json` and report the exact provider-acceptance fact/protocol, final-admission proof rule, sibling-batch evaluation rule, and revocation sort keys that close them.

Verify by targeted text inspection that provider acceptance survives projection rebuild and the provider-response crash boundary for both legacy and new deliveries; current `sent` rows have an explicit cutover disposition; ambiguous historic admission provenance becomes `unproved`; all valid sibling candidates can append grants in one batch; and every revocation consequence class has deterministic total order.
Verify every relative Markdown link in `docs/adr/0025-use-first-class-group-memberships-and-member-owned-conversation-subscriptions.md` resolves to an existing repository path.
completion_evidence_required: Return the exact changed path and confirm no code, migration, test, feature, design, ADR-index, iteration plan, todo, or other project-document path changed.

Name the replayable provider-acceptance mechanism and explain owner, payload, provider-call/local-persistence ordering, idempotent retry, crash recovery, projection rebuild, and legacy cutover treatment.
State the durable temporal predicate that proves a historic follow belongs to the final uninterrupted legacy admission, including remove/re-add and ambiguous/incomparable outcomes.
Describe the atomic sibling-candidate evaluation and deterministic grant/marker order, and explain why the first reconciled provenance cannot suppress later valid siblings.
List the complete revocation append sequence and total sort key for every repeated consequence class, especially prepared-intent cancellations and authorization-end facts.
Report successful whitespace, scope, required-contract, and relative-link validations with exit statuses.
